messages.message:
Patch Set 1:

AI code review results below, please doublecheck

Looks good; no need to re-spin. (suggestion) There is no test for the new behaviour. sanity test_120b ("Early Lock Cancel: create test") already checks the ELC and blocking-AST counters around a create. A sibling test could open(O_CREAT) a LUSTRE_VOLATILE_HDR name in a directory whose UPDATE lock is cached, then check that the parent's mdc lock is still cached and that no cancel or blocking AST was sent. That would catch a later change that brings the cancel back. Fine to add with the llapi patch in this series or on a refresh.

Patch Set 1: Code-Review+1

Looks good to me. I checked that the parent really does not change for a volatile create, so keeping the UPDATE lock is safe:
- mdt_open_lock_mode() returns LCK_NL for MDS_OPEN_VOLATILE, so the MDT takes no lock on the parent.
- In mdd_create(), a volatile file goes to the orphan directory (mdd_orphan_insert) and skips both the index insert in the parent and the parent mtime/ctime update. So the parent's entries and attributes that the UPDATE lock covers stay the same.
- On the client, MDS_CREATE_VOLATILE is set only by ll_prep_md_op_data() for LUSTRE_OPC_CREATE with a volatile name, so normal creates still cancel the lock.
- With an MDT older than 2.14.52, the MDT still locks the parent and sends a blocking callback, the same as a create without early lock cancel. Slower, but correct.

I agree with the AI review that a small test next to sanity test_120b would be good, in this change or in 70665.

commit.subject: LU-21177 mdc: keep parent UPDATE lock for volatile create
commit.message:
LU-21177 mdc: keep parent UPDATE lock for volatile create

mdc_intent_open_pack() cancels the client's UPDATE lock on the
parent directory by early lock cancel before every create. A
volatile file is not linked into its parent, and since 2.14.52
(LU-14693) the MDT takes no DLM lock on the parent for it, so the
lock stays valid and the cancel only costs: it runs
ll_prune_negative_children(), which walks all cached children of
the parent under its d_lock. Tools working by FID (lfs migrate,
lfs mirror extend or split on .lustre/fid/[FID]) create their
volatile files in .lustre/fid, which caches one dentry per FID
looked up. With 400k of them, one volatile create spends about
5 ms in the walk, and path walks through .lustre/fid on the same
client spin on its d_lock meanwhile.

Do not cancel the parent's UPDATE lock for a volatile create. An
older MDT still locks the parent and revokes the lock by a
blocking callback, as for any create without early lock cancel.

Users of liblustreapi's volatile helpers, such as the HSM copytool
restore, also unlink the volatile name after the open, which
cancels the lock in mdc_unlink(). The change "llapi: don't unlink
volatile file opened on Lustre" removes that unlink.

Fixes: 8c04afb5236f ("LU-14693 mdt: skip DLM when opening volatile files")
Signed-off-by: Markus Hilger <markus.hilger@megware.com>
